thread:
alex: Heads-up — scheduled candidate for Senior Backend on Wed 2026-03-25 10:00-11:00 PT. Can the panel (riley, morgan, jamie) confirm availability? Invite sent: https://calendar.example/evt/1839001111 :calendar:
riley: I'm available, will take system design portion.
morgan: I can make that time. Quick rubric question — how should we weight 'architecture depth' vs 'implementation detail'? The rubric on Confluence shows the criteria but not relative weighting.
jamie: I might need to swap out if the QA sync runs long. If someone can cover hands-on, I can take system design.
alex: Good call — our plan was roughly 60% architecture / 40% implementation on the final score. The debrief form has separate fields for 'Depth' and 'Practicality' so you can score both. Debrief link: https://debriefs.example/form/1839001111 :link:
morgan: That helps, thanks. One more — are we expecting any live coding or just a design + pseudo-code walkthrough?
riley: Expect a 25m architecture whiteboard + a ~20m hands-on design prompt (no full coding required, pseudo-code or sketches ok).
people-ops-bot: Reminder: Please submit the debrief within 48 hours after the interview. See policy: https://hr.example/debrief-policy :memo:
jamie: If @morgan is fine swapping, I can take the hands-on. @alex can you update the invite roles?
morgan: I'm good to switch to system design. @jamie take the hands-on.
alex: Done — roles updated on the invite and description. Also added a short prompt in the docs: https://docs.example/hiring/senior-backend/interview-pack.
riley: Sharing a short debrief template to speed things up: ``Strengths:
- ...
Areas to improve:
- ...
Recommendation (Hire/No-hire/Maybe):
Score: Design X/4, Implementation Y/4``
people-ops-bot: Note: If candidate requires budget approval for level, tag #hiring-budget in the debrief thread.
jamie: Thanks — I've got it on my calendar and the invite updated.
alex: Great — I'll send a quick pre-interview note to the candidate and remind the panel the day before. :thumbsup:
